Subject: Proposed compromise language and evidence SLA

Team / Daniel —

I reviewed Horus's redline and drafted a proposed compromise. Summary of the trade:

1) Defense control: Redwood will retain the right to assume and control the defense of any third-party IP claim. If Redwood elects not to assume defense within 15 business days after written notice, Horus may assume defense subject to Redwood's right to approve counsel (approval not to be unreasonably withheld). If Horus assumes defense, Redwood may participate at its own cost.

2) Customer-supplied content carveout: Claims that arise solely from Horus-supplied customer content remain Horus's responsibility (Horus to defend and indemnify). If the claim arises from a combination of Redwood product/service and customer content, parties will allocate based on the primary proximate cause.

3) Counsel rates and oversight: Redwood will not unreasonably withhold approval of Horus's counsel but proposes a guideline cap at $350/hour for lead counsel; parties will reasonably cooperate on fee arrangements.

4) Evidence & retention: Redwood will designate a single evidence liaison (Operations Legal: evidence@redwood.com) and commits to retain logs and relevant artifacts for 12 months after notice of claim where reasonably necessary for defense. Emergency preservation requests will be handled on a best-efforts basis.

5) Settlement and reservation: Redwood will not settle any claim that imposes an obligation on Horus without Horus's prior written consent; Horus will not unreasonably withhold consent.

Attached: proposed-indemnity-language.docx (clean text of the clause).

If Horus is comfortable with this structure, Ben's team can select a commercial concession (credit or temporary cap increase) to sweeten the deal. From a legal risk view, the approach limits Redwood's exposure while giving Horus practical options if Redwood declines to defend.

Jordan Blake
Senior Corporate Counsel
Redwood Inference
